subject: Budgeted hiring roadmap: runtime & infra (Dec-Jan hires)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Budgeted hiring roadmap: runtime & infra (Dec-Jan hires)

Team —

I'm sharing the proposed, budgeted roadmap for runtime & infra headcount we want to commit to for the next two hiring windows (Dec hiring window + Jan start dates). This version ties each req to a costed FTE line (salary + benefits + recruiting fee) and the proposed comp band to use when closing. File attached: 2026-Q4-hiring-slate.xlsx and comp-bands-runtime-v2.pdf.

Summary (high level):
- 4 backend/runtime engineers (2 senior ICs, 2 mid) — prioritized for low-latency critical paths
- 1 infra reliability engineer (senior) — paging and autoscaling work
- 1 quant/ops engineer (mid) — model compilation/runtime perf work

Why now: the new model sharding changes and next-gen KV cache work require extra runway to avoid a 3–4 month delivery hit. We also have two high-priority customer commitments for Dedicated capacity that require predictable throughput.

Asks:
- Approval to open all 6 reqs against the Q4 budget today.
- One comp-band exception (if needed) for the infra reliability senior role — details below.
- Connor: prioritization guidance if finance pushes back.
- Laura: can you confirm runway/bench funds for hiring fees and target month to onboard?

Notes on comp-band exception: Marcus flagged that the market for senior infra reliability is hotter than our current band; we may need to go ~10% above published band to secure someone with on-call + kernel experience. See comp-bands-runtime-v2.pdf, section 3.

If I don't hear objections, I'll kick off req creation and loop TalentBridge for active sourcing Monday.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Platform Staffing (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-Q4-hiring-slate.xlsx (spreadsheet), comp-bands-runtime-v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Budgeted hiring roadmap: runtime & infra (Dec-Jan hires)

Kim — thanks for the packet. Quick notes inline and a couple of asks: 

- I agree we should prioritize the two senior ICs first; the mid hires can be backfilled in quarter if the external candidate funnel is thin.
- If we have to pick one role to defer, I recommend deferring the quant/ops mid until Q1 rather than the infra senior — the reliability gaps will increase our incident MTTR.
- For the comp-band exception: provide a short one-paragraph rationale we can present to the compensation committee. Marcus, can you draft?

Also, headcount cadence note: if we open all 6 now, recruiting bandwidth will be the gating factor. Suggest we request a 2-week sourcing premium from TalentBridge (extra 1 sourcer) for the month of December.

Connor
Director, Runtime Engineering

Subject: Re: Budgeted hiring roadmap: runtime & infra (Dec-Jan hires)

Kim / all —

I drafted the comp-band exception note (short rationale) and attached a benchmark snippet to justify the +10% over band. Quick summary:
- Role: Senior Infra Reliability Engineer (on-call + kernel/driver exposure)
- Market note: three recent offers (two Bay Area, one EU remote) paid ~8–12% above our Level 5 band for like-for-like candidates
- Business impact: fill closes a long tail of infra tech debt and reduces projected incident costs by estimated $320k/yr if we avoid a major outage.

Attached: comp-bands-runtime-v2.pdf (section 3 excerpt). OK to escalate this to compensation committee tomorrow if we get finance signoff on headcount.

-Marcus
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Budgeted hiring roadmap: runtime & infra (Dec-Jan hires)

Kim —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Finance run-rate check: we have budget capacity to onboard 4 full-cost FTEs in Dec/Jan without drawing down contingency, provided recruiting fees are capped at 20%/hire. That covers the two seniors + two mids. 

If we proceed with 6 hires now (including the infra senior exception), we will need to pull $180k from contingency to cover fees and signing variance. That is doable but requires Exec approval for the comp-band exception and a finance-side note committing to the incremental spend.

Practical ask from Finance:
- Kimberly: please attach a one-page business impact statement per exception (Marcus' short rationale is a good start).
- Connor: confirm we want the sourcing premium (it adds $36k in agency fees).

If we don't get exec approval by Thurs (12/3), we should stagger openings: open 4 reqs now and queue the infra senior for the next window.

—Laura
Head of Finance, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Folks —

Thanks for the quick turn. Plan of record based on the thread:
1) Open 4 reqs today (two senior ICs, two mid) against the budgeted lines. Recruiting to start Mon.
2) Prepare the comp-band exception one-pager for Execs (Marcus to finalize rationale; I will format and add the estimated mitigation numbers Laura requested).
3) Hold the infra reliability senior role pending Exec approval; target decision by Thu 12/3.
4) Connor, please confirm the sourcing premium by EOD so TalentBridge can scope resourcing.

Sarah — looping you in for sourcing scope & timeline. Please confirm whether TalentBridge can provide the extra sourcer and an estimated ETA to send first shortlists.

I'll circulate a final one-pager + ask to the compensation committee Wednesday morning.

Kim
Kimberly Park
